      "observations": [
        "All 638 owned diff lines across nine paths were read, including the full deleted native implementation/header, full new JS module and each native/build/registration edit. The contract string stays the same, the CID and component implementation change, native storage becomes nsCOMPtr<msgIPasswordAuthModule>, and the module is packaged through EXTRA_JS_MODULES. Registration source is not a successful build or instance-creation result.",
        "The JavaScript port uses asynchronous search/removal internally, but public manager-query/forget methods remain synchronous event-loop bridges. The original manager-query wrapper does not return its internal result; the accepted later wrapper explicitly returns the cache. Existing focused lesson 77345e8a already covers synchronous waiting and lookup-miss/cache separation, so it is linked rather than recreated. The unchanged scriptable IDL and actual native caller preserve the cross-language return contract.",
        "The original IMAP AsyncGetPassword port replaces the old nonempty-cache assignment guard with if (value.IsEmpty()), so it assigns an empty value and does not assign a nonempty value through that branch. The accepted counterpart restores !value.IsEmpty(). The actual protocol consumer checks whether immediate output is empty before waiting for a prompt result, shutdown or cancellation. This is an exact static branch difference, not an observed hang or proven regression cause.",
        "The native forget loop ignored removal failure and continued to clear its cache. The new async JS loop retains the comment saying to continue and clear cache if removal fails, but awaits removeLoginAsync with no local catch; rejection exits before cache clearing. The accepted reused snapshot retains that mismatch. No failure injection or password-store state was executed.",
        "The JS forget match also accepts username.slice(0, username.indexOf(\"@\")) without guarding for a missing @. In JavaScript a -1 endpoint removes the last code unit, so a distinct stored login matching that shortened name can satisfy the alternative. This is the exact expression and candidate scope, not a claimed native-equivalence proof or account-isolation test.",
        "The port changes user cancellation from the native special successful NS_MSG_PASSWORD_PROMPT_CANCELLED result to throwing NS_ERROR_ABORT in JS; the IDL still describes the special-success contract. The accepted module later adds key/private cache/notification support and an explicit query return. The Exchange class is later renamed and adds NTLM to its manager-load branch. These later source facts are separate and are not credited as part of this original port. No test or assertion body changes in this entry.",
        "Complete own review D295233 has sparse approval, then a failed remote build, later update/completion and landing. It has no actual inlines or summary edits. Shared full primary is reused from the one complete family read; the later missed Rust caller and admitted new test failure remain distinct from these native/JS interfaces.",
        "The complete own review contains no submitted inlines or summary histories. Its sparse approval precedes a failed build, later update/completion and landing. The author explicitly describes temporary fake asynchronicity, consistent with the exact synchronous interface bridges; there is no Promise-returning public API or fresh build claim.",
        "Shared complete primary 1985223 is reused from B's one family read and original A capture, with original scope/time unchanged. The later missed Rust caller/reopening and test-failure report are separate; no new independent primary confirmation is claimed."
